title: Rectangles, Rhombuses and Squares
short: Equal diagonals mean a rectangle; perpendicular diagonals mean a rhombus.
trouble: Students think a quadrilateral with perpendicular diagonals must be a rhombus.

blocks.html: Three kinds of parallelograms get their own names. A rectangle has four right angles. A rhombus has four congruent sides. A square is both. Each one has every property from Properties of Parallelograms, plus more, and those extra properties give new tests like the ones in Proving a Quadrilateral Is a Parallelogram.

Rectangle diagonals are congruent. In rectangle $ABCD$, $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle DCB$ share $\overline{BC}$, have $AB = DC$, and have right angles at $B$ and $C$. By SAS they are congruent, so $AC = DB$.
Rhombus diagonals are perpendicular. In rhombus $ABCD$ with diagonals meeting at $E$, $\triangle AEB \cong \triangle CEB$ by SSS ($AB = CB$, $AE = CE$, shared $\overline{BE}$). So the angles at $E$ are congruent, and since they form a linear pair, each is $90^\circ$. The same triangles show that each diagonal bisects the angles it passes through.

blocks.cap: Diagonal properties and tests. The tests apply only to a figure already known to be a parallelogram.

blocks.html: Rectangles have congruent diagonals; rhombuses have perpendicular diagonals that bisect the angles; squares have both. A parallelogram with congruent diagonals is a rectangle, and one with perpendicular diagonals is a rhombus.

blocks.title: Rectangle diagonals
blocks.q: $ABCD$ is a rectangle with $AC = 4x - 6$ and $BD = 2x + 10$. Find $AC$.

blocks.title: A rhombus side from its diagonals
blocks.q: A rhombus has diagonals of length $10$ and $24$. Find the length of a side.
steps: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making four right triangles with legs $5$ and $12$.

blocks.title: A rhombus angle
blocks.q: In rhombus $PQRS$, $m\angle QPR = (3x + 2)^\circ$ and $m\angle SPR = (5x - 14)^\circ$. Find $m\angle QPS$.

blocks.html: Deciding that any quadrilateral with perpendicular diagonals is a rhombus. A kite has perpendicular diagonals too, and it is not a parallelogram at all. The test "perpendicular diagonals means rhombus" only works once you know the figure is a parallelogram. Check that first.
